entry.title: The Foom Cash Exploit: How a Skipped CLI Step in a Groth16 Trusted Setup Turned a $2.3M Privacy Protocol Into an ATM
entry.summary:
TL;DR
On March 2, 2026, attackers drained $2.26M from Foom Cash — a zk-SNARK privacy protocol on Ethereum and Base — by forging zero-knowledge proofs. The root cause? A single omitted step during the Groth16 trusted setup that left γ and δ parameters at their default generator values, collapsing the entire soundness guarantee of the proof system. A white-hat rescue recovered $1.84M (81%) through front-running the attacker with the same forged-proof technique. This article dissects the vulnerability, the proof malleability exploit, and what every team deploying ZK circuits needs to learn from it.
